newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank may sell gov't securities unit.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank may sell gov't securities unit.

text.p: NationsBank Corp on Wednesday said it was considering selling its profitable U.S. government securities primary-dealer operation.
NationsBank in a statement also denied a Bloomberg Business News report that it was selling its foreign exchange business.

The company said the sale of the U.S. government securities operation, which trades government securities for its clients as well as its own accounts, would allow NationsBank to grow while "potentially freeing up resources needed to support our core corporate customer franchise."
J.P. Morgan is assisting NationsBank with the sale, a NationsBank spokeswoman said. She would not comment on whether there were any negotiations about the sale currently under way.

NationsBanc Capital Markets, the fixed-income and investment banking unit of NationsBank, will meet the needs of institutional investors and clients for such services through its existing capital markets infrastructure in Charlotte and Chicago, it said.
Regarding the foreign exchange business, the company said, "The FX business is absolutely not for sale. In 1996, we refined this business, and we are extremely pleased with its performance."
